findings.title: Feature-flagged table branch renders a hardcoded empty table
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the organization has the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` — completely ignoring the actual `tableResults`, `loading` state, `fields`, field aliases, and custom renderers. If this flag is ever enabled for an organization, every table widget on their dashboards will render an empty table with no columns and no data instead of the query results, with no loading or error states. If this is intentional scaffolding, the flag must remain off until real data is wired through; otherwise this branch needs to pass the actual result data before merging.

findings.title: Custom cell renderers checked by truthiness instead of undefined, so falsy React nodes are discarded
findings.body: In both `renderDefaultBodyCell` (line 70) and `renderDefaultHeadCell` (line 31), the custom renderer result is checked with `if (cell) { return cell; }`. The documented contract (in the component docstrings and stories) is that the fallback renderer only runs when the custom renderer returns `undefined`. A custom renderer that legitimately returns a falsy React node — e.g. `0`, `''`, or `false` — will be silently ignored and replaced by the default renderer, producing wrong cell content. The check should be `if (cell !== undefined)` (or `!= null`) to match the documented behavior.
